points.description: States that a tree is a collection of nodes with one special node called the root, and the remaining nodes are partitioned into one or more disjoint sets, each of which is itself a tree (recursive definition).
points.partial_credit: 2 marks for giving only part: e.g. a collection of nodes with a root, but no mention of the remaining nodes forming disjoint subtrees; or vague/minor error in wording.

points.description: Includes the distinct detail that the subsets/subtrees are disjoint (no node shared between them) and that each is itself a tree.
points.partial_credit: Half a mark if only 'subtrees' or 'children' is mentioned without disjointness or the recursive point.

rubric.notes: Full marks for stating a tree is a collection of nodes with a root, whose remaining nodes split into disjoint sets that are each trees, in any wording. Part marks for a root plus nodes/subtrees stated vaguely, or with a minor error. No marks for describing only related ideas (e.g. hierarchical structure, parent-child links, binary trees) without the root and subtree idea.
